en: The last Vault crumbles... Our vessels are reborn, complete once more.
FEAST UPON THEM!
Hehe, another one for the vats...
Specks of light... Contained... Shifting within...
The pain remains... The Seal... Endures...
No... Stay away... Please...
I... can see...
The Light has left.
I am... Hollow.
I have little to give... But it is yours...
The Light surges...
An infiltrator approaches... Yes. An aberration.
I am prepared to serve.
Channel your violent grace onto me. Let it wash over my flesh until it lays seared and pure!
NO... THE CRADLE...  MUST REMAIN...
SISTER... FORGIVE ME...
Dried remains, lingering in perpetuity.
The surface of the stone has taken on a darker hue.
Sacrifice Salt Receptacle
The Faithful
To be born is to be of the faithful.
No god demanded worship of themselves above their siblings, and the faithful would each seek their deity among the pantheon.
But that was long ago. The gods since vanished, and to be faithful is to despair.
Countless fell into bleak sorrow. A few yet linger, trusting that the gods are never truly gone.
They cling to every sign, hoping to be rewarded for their faith.
Calamity
As the Light scorched the world above, the oceans boiled, and the earth crumbled. Life was driven beneath.
To the lament of all, once sunlit and jovial halls were cast into silent darkness. Those who remained fell to their knees, posing questions born of fear and indignation.
They had been dutiful. They had sacrificed. They had eaten. They recited holy words and endured the adjoining hardship.
And yet they were granted no answer. The gods were gone. The City had gone gray and silent.
Hidden Oceans
A glimpse into the minds of gods.
The primeval brine from which the first gods once crawled, and in which life was shaped, nurtured, and punished. What finally rose to its feet in the mud cried out, demanding more.
Now the sea of life lays frozen, its labyrinthian tunnels testament to the workings of long-dead Progenitors.
Their pathways wind as the stalks of minds belonging to creatures far ascended mortality.
Rebirth
The Progenitors crawled through these caverns once. One by one, they emerged, seeking the song that woke them.
Those with sight feared them. Those who heard them succumbed. Those who tasted their Flesh raised tabernacles in their names.
As their following grew, so did their forms. Bloated and full as they became, their shrines could contain them no longer, and the zealots reveled before the end.
Yet, through their demise, the blessed Ichor flowed, and long-dormant husks festered with new life.
Life Before the Star
Above, where the new light bathes all in hues of crimson, we once lived. That is what those who lost themselves say.
The lesson—according to those who rule in the name of the gods—is that faith is not concerned with earthly matters of hearth and home.
Faith alone is where we must live. It is the warmth we require and the shelter we need. To fail this lesson is to be without a place to belong.
If those who lost themselves were ever to reach the surface, they would lament the loss of our city below. They are forever transient in search of a destination they lack the will to find.
The Red Star
The crimson Light danced from the majesty that had pierced the firmament.
Many were so blinded by Its magnificence that they remained until their feet melted into the rock.
Countless joined in bliss, forever remaining in the Light.
It had blessed them for their dedication, re-sculpting them just as it had the world around them. The Light made no distinction.
The Light can still be felt reaching into the stone of the world below.
Outsiders
They came from far away, journeying across the waters on a vessel of steel.
Through the ice they broke, guided beneath the Light, yet they were found lacking in both faith and understanding.
Some ventured below in search of salvation, yet their avarice would not permit them such.
Within the ice, the beast has remained, festering with confusion wrought by the ignorant.
The merging of god and steel.
Journey's End
The bloated beast lay dying within the ice, struggling to breathe, unable to carry its masters further.
Its steel hide had been struck and tortured, seared by flame, and pierced by jagged nails. Blackened blood seeped into the stone below.
The cries that once reverberated through its veins grew hollow, replaced by a dull patting against its skin.
As it lay at the brink of death, an unfamiliar voice called out from within. Life returned to its scorched shell, and the metal began to sing.
Cultivation
The soil of the city was fertile and eager to be cultivated. So it was that the people gathered in the fields, offering seeds of the gods to the earth.
They watered them with holy secretions, drained directly from the bodies of their benevolent deities, and waited in anticipation for signs of growth.
Plants, trees, and flora soon burst into life, and the great Gardens were born. Their plateaus provided all with food, shade, and most importantly, the possibility for growth.
Those who tended the vibrant groves turned their minds towards the future. Great works of alchemy were conducted, ensuring that the cycle of life left nothing to spoil.
The Vats
The alchemists of the Gardens watched their cultivations grow, and lamented.
They understood what would sprout, when it would grow, and what each bud would unveil. The Gardens, the living jewel of the city, had become stagnant, devoid of change.
In time, they called the first of the anointed to bring her teachings to the plateaus, to further their creations for the benefit of all.
By their hands, the great vats were constructed, and the husks of the dead were granted new purpose.
Life was created.
A Child Is Born
As the Red Star rose above, a royal heir was held up to receive its blessed Light—a miracle birthed from the barren womb of an aged queen. The Court reveled.
The king decreed that delights should be brought from the far reaches of the world, by ship and by caravan, to please the young heir.
Yet none seemed to sustain the child. No exotic fruits, spiced meats, nor sweet nectar nourished him. He remained malcontent, his body weak and slowly wasting.
Desperate, the king and queen beseeched the gods for aid and brought their blessed Flesh before the Court.
From that day forth, the child became the epitome of joy, his belly round and full.
Lack of Faith
These enclosed halls stand as a testament to the cowardice uncertainty provokes.
As the city collapsed into the earth, the people screamed and wailed. They hid behind thick doors and walls of stone, hoping to avoid calamity, trusting only that which they could see and touch.
Their lack of devotion would not go unpunished.
In the same cold dark in which they cowered, something began to stir. Ancient fauna, brought to the great Court from many lands all across the world, grew strange, transforming into something new.
The faithless became sustenance for those who dared to change their fates, and now, forever, stand as husks—eerie but beautiful testaments to their lack of faith.
To Know All
Existence is simple to those of simple minds, and knowing remains disjointed from understanding.
Few are those who can truly perceive the strings that lead between worlds—the net that encompasses all.
Yet there are those for whom such concepts appear as but a natural part of being, an unseen guiding hand steering others towards the ever-expanding borders of the known.
Some do come to see, to share their pursuits, as halls of endless knowledge beckon the ambitious and foolish alike.
Memories
All of my memories.
I remember them perfectly. The sky above. The tall spires. The dazzling vistas in every direction.
I remember most of it. A city spanning so vast it put even nature to shame, dwarfing forests, lakes, and mountains.
I remember some of it. Hazy mists obscuring what lies below. Stone, metal, and wood, but no faces. No movements.
I barely remember any of it. Muffled sounds. Dull colors. The absence of life.
I have forgotten.
Stars Without Number
